library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Samuels_2025_infliximab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Samuels_2025_infliximab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70086> (open access; Data S1 holds
  Table S1 and the NONMEM code used for the predictions)
* Structural model: Xiong 2021, <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.2148>

```{r load-model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Samuels_2025_infliximab"))
```

Samuels 2025 asks a dosing question. Infliximab clearance in children with
Crohn's disease depends on body weight, serum albumin, the erythrocyte
sedimentation rate (ESR) and the neutrophil CD64 activity ratio (nCD64), and
those biomarkers improve as the patient responds to induction. A dose chosen
from pre-treatment values therefore over-predicts clearance for the rest of
induction. The paper fits a log-scale Emax function of the infusion number to
each biomarker and plugs the predicted values into the Xiong 2021 population
PK model, whose parameters it holds at the published estimates.

# Population

The biomarker trajectories were estimated on 239 children and young adults
with Crohn's disease starting infliximab in two US cohorts (Samuels 2025
Table 1). REFINE (n = 78) was a prospective multicentre observational study at
four centres from 2014 to 2019. APPDASH (n = 161) was a retrospective cohort at
Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center from 2019 to 2021. Mean age at the
first infusion was 13.6 (SD 3.7) years and 92.1% were under 18; 40.6% were
female and 86.6% White. The mean starting dose was 7.7 (SD 2.3) mg/kg, higher in
APPDASH (8.2) than in REFINE (6.5). Mean biomarkers at the first infusion were:
weight 48.3 kg, albumin 3.3 g/dL, ESR 26 mm/h and nCD64 7.2.

The PK parameters themselves are not re-estimated here. They come from Xiong
2021, which fitted 671 peak and trough concentrations from the 78 REFINE
patients.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Samuels_2025_infliximab")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every value in `ini()` carries an in-file comment naming its source. In
summary:

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| CL (65 kg, ALB 3.5 g/dL, ESR 9 mm/h, nCD64 4.6) | 0.0138 L/h | Data S1 THETA(1); Xiong 2021 Table 2 |
| V1 (65 kg) | 2.97 L | Data S1 THETA(2); Xiong 2021 Table 2 |
| Q (65 kg) | 0.00953 L/h | Data S1 THETA(3); Xiong 2021 Table 2 (0.0095) |
| V2 (65 kg) | 2.84 L | Data S1 THETA(4); Xiong 2021 Table 2 |
| Albumin exponent on CL | -1.07 | Data S1 THETA(5); Xiong 2021 Table 2 |
| ATI exponent on CL (above 22 ng/mL) | 0.134 | Data S1 THETA(6) and `IF(ATI.LE.22)` branch; Xiong 2021 Table 2 |
| nCD64 exponent on CL | 0.168 | Data S1 THETA(7); Xiong 2021 Table 2 |
| ESR exponent on CL | 0.101 | Data S1 THETA(8); Xiong 2021 Table 2 |
| Weight exponent on CL | 0.594 | Data S1 THETA(9) 'CLWT1'; Xiong 2021 Table 2 (see Assumptions) |
| Weight exponent on V1 | 0.55 | Data S1 THETA(10) 'V1WT1'; Xiong 2021 Table 2 |
| Weight exponents on Q and V2 | 1 and 0.586 | Data S1 `$PK` code; Xiong 2021 Table 2 |
| Emax, weight | 0.046 | Table S1; Data S1 E2; Results; Figure 1a |
| Emax, albumin | 0.110 | Table S1; Data S1 E1; Results; Figure 1b |
| Emax, ESR | -0.978 | Table S1; Data S1 E3; Results; Figure 1c |
| Emax, nCD64 | -0.362 | Table S1; Data S1 E4; Results; Figure 1d |
| D50 | 1.1 (held) | Methods; Data S1 constant 0.1 = D50 - 1 |
| IIV on CL | 0.0629 | Data S1 OMEGA(1,1); Xiong 2021 Table 2 (25.1% CV) |
| IIV on V1, Q, V2 | 0 (omitted) | Data S1 OMEGA(2)-(4) |
| Residual SD, log scale | sqrt(0.189) = 0.4347 | Data S1 `$SIGMA`; Xiong 2021 Table 2 (0.435) |
| Trajectory equation | biomarker = E0 * exp(Emax * (n - 1) / (D50 - 1 + n - 1)) | Methods equation; Data S1 E1-E4 |
| CL equation | power product of the predicted biomarkers and thresholded ATI | Data S1 `$PK`; Xiong 2021 Table 2 footnote |
| Residual model | Y = log(F) + EPS | Data S1 `$ERROR` |

# Biomarker trajectories (Figure 1)

The Emax function predicts each biomarker from its pre-treatment value at
infusion number `n`. Because the D50 of 1.1 sits just above the first
infusion, nearly the whole change, 1 / 1.1 = 91% of it, is in place by the
second infusion.

```{r fig1}
theta <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Samuels_2025_infliximab"))$theta
e0 <- c(
  "Weight (kg)" = 48.8, "Albumin (g/dL)" = 3.3,
  "ESR (mm/h)" = 27.6, "nCD64 (ratio)" = 7.7
)
emax <- c(
  "Weight (kg)" = theta[["wt_dosenum_max"]],
  "Albumin (g/dL)" = theta[["alb_dosenum_max"]],
  "ESR (mm/h)" = theta[["esr_dosenum_max"]],
  "nCD64 (ratio)" = theta[["neutrophil_cd64_ratio_dosenum_max"]]
)
d50 <- theta[["dosenum50"]]
traj <- expand.grid(n = seq(1, 4, by = 0.01), biomarker = names(e0)) |>
  mutate(
    value = e0[as.character(biomarker)] *
      exp(emax[as.character(biomarker)] * (n - 1) / (d50 - 1 + n - 1))
  )
ggplot(traj, aes(n, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~biomarker, scales = "free_y") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(
    x = "Dose number", y = "Predicted biomarker",
    caption = "Replicates the fitted curves of Figure 1 of Samuels 2025 (E0 from Table S1)."
  )
```

The Results quote each Emax as an asymptotic percentage change,
`exp(Emax) - 1`. Three of the four reproduce:

```{r fig1-check}
pct_chk <- data.frame(
  biomarker = names(emax),
  row.names = NULL,
  paper_pct = c(4.7, 11.7, -62.4, -26.5),
  model_pct = unname(round(100 * (exp(emax) - 1), 1))
)
knitr::kable(pct_chk |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Biomarker = biomarker,
    "Results / Figure 1 (%)" = paper_pct,
    "100 * (exp(Emax) - 1) (%)" = model_pct
  ))
stopifnot(all(abs(pct_chk$model_pct[1:3] - pct_chk$paper_pct[1:3]) < 0.2))
```

The nCD64 Emax of -0.362 gives -30.4%, not the -26.5% printed in the Results
and in the Figure 1d title. The value -0.362 is printed in three places (Table
S1, the Data S1 code and the Figure 1d title), so it is the one encoded. The
-26.5% matches neither the estimate nor the bootstrap median (-0.404), and is
treated as a typographical error in the percentage.

# Figure 2: a 47 kg patient on 5 or 10 mg/kg

Samuels 2025 Figure 2 simulates infusions at weeks 0, 2, 6 and 14 for a
47 kg patient, with and without the predicted biomarker improvement. The
paper does not state the other pre-treatment biomarkers used, so the Table S1
E0 values (albumin 3.3 g/dL, ESR 27.6 mm/h, nCD64 7.7) are used here, with no
antibodies to infliximab.

## How the infusion counter is set

`CYCLE` is the 1-based infusion number, and the model forms the paper's
zero-based `INFUSION = CYCLE - 1`. The Emax equation defines a biomarker value
at each infusion visit but not between visits. Figure 2 shows the two curves
separating before the second infusion. That is the NONMEM convention in which
a record's covariates govern the interval that ends at that record: the
interval after infusion `k` takes the biomarker values of visit `k + 1`. In
rxode2, which carries covariates forward, the same thing is done by giving
every record after infusion `k` the value `CYCLE = k + 1`. For the
baseline-only prediction, `CYCLE` stays at 1 throughout.

```{r fig2-events}
dose_wk <- c(0, 2, 6, 14)
dose_h <- dose_wk * 7 * 24
inf_dur <- 2 # h; the paper does not state the infusion duration
obs_h <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 22 * 168, by = 6), dose_h + inf_dur)))

make_events <- function(id, mgkg, scenario, wt = 47, alb_gdl = 3.3,
                        esr = 27.6, ncd64 = 7.7, ada = 0) {
  amt <- mgkg * wt
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = dose_h, amt = amt, rate = amt / inf_dur,
    evid = 1L, cmt = "central"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = obs_h, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central"
  )
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  # Closing-visit convention: after infusion k, CYCLE = k + 1.
  ev$CYCLE <- if (scenario == "Time-varying biomarkers") {
    findInterval(ev$time, dose_h) + 1L
  } else {
    1L
  }
  ev$WT <- wt
  ev$ALB <- alb_gdl * 10 # g/dL -> canonical g/L
  ev$ESR <- esr
  ev$NEUTROPHIL_CD64_RATIO <- ncd64
  ev$CONC_ADA_NGML <- ada
  ev$treatment <- paste0(mgkg, " mg/kg")
  ev$scenario <- scenario
  ev
}

scen <- c("Time-varying biomarkers", "Baseline biomarkers only")
ev_fig2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(1, 5, scen[1]), make_events(2, 5, scen[2]),
  make_events(3, 10, scen[1]), make_events(4, 10, scen[2])
)
sim_fig2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_fig2,
  keep = c("treatment", "scenario"), returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r fig2-plot, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(sim_fig2, aes(time / 168, Cc, linetype = scenario, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, NA)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 22, by = 2)) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, ncol = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("black", "purple")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Infliximab (ug/mL)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Samuels 2025 (typical patient, no IIV)."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Troughs read from Figure 2a (5 mg/kg) by the maintainers, against the
simulation:

```{r fig2-troughs}
trough_h <- c(2, 6, 14) * 168
fig2 <- data.frame(
  week = c(2, 6, 14),
  paper_tv = c(16.0, 12.8, 4.7),
  paper_base = c(12.8, 8.6, 2.6)
)
sim_tr <- sim_fig2 |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "5 mg/kg", time %in% trough_h) |>
  dplyr::mutate(week = time / 168) |>
  dplyr::select(week, scenario, Cc) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = Cc)
fig2_cmp <- fig2 |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_tr, by = "week") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    paper_ratio = paper_tv / paper_base,
    sim_ratio = `Time-varying biomarkers` / `Baseline biomarkers only`
  )
knitr::kable(
  fig2_cmp |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Week (trough)" = week,
      "Figure 2a, time-varying" = paper_tv,
      "Figure 2a, baseline only" = paper_base,
      "Model, time-varying" = `Time-varying biomarkers`,
      "Model, baseline only" = `Baseline biomarkers only`,
      "Figure 2a ratio" = paper_ratio,
      "Model ratio" = sim_ratio
    ),
  digits = 2
)
```

The ratio of the two predictions is the quantity the paper is about. It
depends on the Emax trajectories and the covariate exponents, not on the dose
or on the unreported baseline biomarkers, and the model reproduces it closely.
The week-2 ratio is the one most sensitive to how the counter is stepped
within the first interval, which the paper does not describe.

```{r fig2-assert}
stopifnot(all(abs(log(fig2_cmp$sim_ratio[2:3] / fig2_cmp$paper_ratio[2:3])) < log(1.1)))
```

Both absolute curves sit 10-30% below the figure. With linear PK and a
ratio that agrees, the gap points to lower clearance in the paper's typical
patient, most likely from pre-treatment ESR and nCD64 values below the Table S1
means (for example cohort medians, which the paper does not report). Setting
every biomarker to its reference value instead puts the baseline-only troughs
above the figure (15.0, 10.7 and 3.7 ug/mL), so the figure's patient lies
between the two.

# Virtual cohort and Table 3

Table 3 of Samuels 2025 compares observed troughs with population predictions
from the baseline biomarkers (scenario a) and from the predicted trajectories
(scenario b). The virtual cohort below draws pre-treatment biomarkers and
starting doses from the Table 1 means and SDs. The doses and sampling of the
real patients are not available, so the absolute medians are approximate. The
ratio of scenario b to scenario a is the comparison that carries over.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20250222)
n_sub <- 200
lnorm_draw <- function(n, m, s) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (s / m)^2))
  rlnorm(n, log(m) - sdlog^2 / 2, sdlog)
}
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  wt = pmin(pmax(lnorm_draw(n_sub, 48.3, 20.5), 15), 120),
  alb = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 3.3, 0.61), 1.5), 5),
  esr = pmax(lnorm_draw(n_sub, 26, 24), 1),
  ncd64 = pmax(lnorm_draw(n_sub, 7.2, 4.6), 1),
  mgkg = round(pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 7.7, 2.3), 5), 10))
)

trough_events <- function(row, scenario, id) {
  amt <- row$mgkg * row$wt
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = dose_h, amt = amt, rate = amt / inf_dur,
    evid = 1L, cmt = "central"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = trough_h - 0.01, amt = 0, rate = 0,
    evid = 0L, cmt = "central"
  )
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  ev$CYCLE <- if (scenario == "b") findInterval(ev$time, dose_h) + 1L else 1L
  ev$WT <- row$wt
  ev$ALB <- row$alb * 10
  ev$ESR <- row$esr
  ev$NEUTROPHIL_CD64_RATIO <- row$ncd64
  ev$CONC_ADA_NGML <- 0
  ev$scenario <- scenario
  ev
}
ev_cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    trough_events(cohort[i, ], "a", i),
    trough_events(cohort[i, ], "b", n_sub + i)
  )
}))
sim_cohort <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_cohort,
  keep = "scenario", returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose = c(2, 3, 4)[match(round(time), round(trough_h - 0.01))])

tab3 <- data.frame(
  dose = c(2, 3, 4),
  observed = c(22, 19, 7.1),
  paper_a = c(12.8, 10.7, 4.9),
  paper_b = c(17.7, 16.9, 8.5)
)
sim_tab3 <- sim_cohort |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose, scenario) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_cc = median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = median_cc, names_prefix = "sim_")
sub_ratio <- sim_cohort |>
  dplyr::mutate(subj = ifelse(scenario == "b", id - n_sub, id)) |>
  dplyr::select(subj, dose, scenario, Cc) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = scenario, values_from = Cc) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim_ratio = median(b / a))
tab3_cmp <- tab3 |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_tab3, by = "dose") |>
  dplyr::left_join(sub_ratio, by = "dose") |>
  dplyr::mutate(paper_ratio = paper_b / paper_a)
knitr::kable(
  tab3_cmp |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Trough before dose" = dose,
      "Observed median" = observed,
      "Table 3, scenario a" = paper_a,
      "Table 3, scenario b" = paper_b,
      "Model median, a" = sim_a,
      "Model median, b" = sim_b,
      "Model median ratio b/a" = sim_ratio,
      "Table 3 ratio b/a" = paper_ratio
    ),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Median trough concentrations (ug/mL), Samuels 2025 Table 3 against the virtual cohort."
)
```

The model's ratio of scenario b to scenario a reproduces Table 3 closely
before the second and third infusions (1.38 and 1.58 in the paper) and is
about 7% higher before the fourth (1.73 in the paper). That comparison sets the
median of per-patient ratios here against a ratio of medians over different
patient subsets in the paper, so agreement within 10-15% is what can be
expected. The absolute medians differ more, because the virtual cohort's doses
and covariates are drawn from Table 1 summaries rather than from the patients
who contributed each trough.

```{r cohort-assert}
stopifnot(
  # Size of the paper's central effect at each of the three troughs.
  all(abs(log(tab3_cmp$sim_ratio / tab3_cmp$paper_ratio)) < log(1.15))
)
```

# Stochastic simulation

With the IIV on clearance and the log-scale residual error, 200 virtual
patients on 5 mg/kg with the time-varying biomarkers:

```{r vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250222)
ev_vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
  ev <- make_events(i, 5, scen[1],
    wt = cohort$wt[i], alb_gdl = cohort$alb[i],
    esr = cohort$esr[i], ncd64 = cohort$ncd64[i]
  )
  ev[ev$evid == 1L | (ev$time %% 24 == 0 & ev$time >= 24), ]
}))
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_vpc, returnType = "data.frame")
vpc_sum <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = quantile(sim, 0.5), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95)
  )
ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(time / 168)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 22, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Infliximab (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles of simulated observations, 200 patients, 5 mg/kg."
  )
```

# PKNCA

Non-compartmental analysis per dosing interval of the Figure 2 typical-patient
simulations. Intervals 2 to 4 close on the week 6, 14 and 22 troughs.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim_fig2 |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = paste(treatment, scenario)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment, scenario)
doses <- ev_fig2 |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = paste(treatment, scenario)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment, scenario)
o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + scenario + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | treatment + scenario + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = dose_h,
  end = c(dose_h[-1], 22 * 168),
  cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(interval = paste0("week ", start / 168, "-", end / 168)) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, scenario, interval, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
knitr::kable(
  nca_tbl |>
    dplyr::rename(
      Dose = treatment, Scenario = scenario, Interval = interval,
      "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax, "AUClast (ug*h/mL)" = auclast,
      "Cmin (ug/mL)" = cmin
    ),
  digits = 1
)
```

Samuels 2025 reports no NCA parameters, so the comparison against the paper is
the Figure 2 and Table 3 trough comparison above. Two properties of the model
are checked here. Because the PK is linear, the 10 mg/kg exposures are exactly
twice the 5 mg/kg ones. And the first-interval Cmax is the same in both
scenarios to within the small change in V1 that the predicted weight gain
causes.

```{r pknca-assert}
auc_ratio <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, scenario, interval, auclast) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = auclast) |>
  dplyr::mutate(r = `10 mg/kg` / `5 mg/kg`)
cmax1 <- nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(interval == "week 0-2", treatment == "5 mg/kg")
stopifnot(
  all(abs(auc_ratio$r - 2) < 1e-3),
  abs(cmax1$cmax[1] / cmax1$cmax[2] - 1) < 0.05
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Weight exponent on CL.** The Data S1 code has a typo in its THETA
  indices. Its non-missing-weight branch is `CLWT=((WT*E2)/65)**THETA(10)`,
  which would use the V1 weight exponent (0.55) on clearance. Its
  missing-weight branch for V1 cites `THETA(11)`, which the `$THETA` block
  (ten entries) does not define. The `$THETA` labels (THETA(9) 'CLWT1' = 0.594,
  THETA(10) 'V1WT1' = 0.55), the missing-weight branch for CL (`E2**THETA(9)`)
  and the Xiong 2021 final model ('Weight for CL' 0.594, 'Weight for V1' 0.55)
  all agree. The model therefore uses 0.594 on CL and 0.55 on V1. The
  difference is small: at 47 kg the CL weight factor is 0.825 with 0.594 and
  0.837 with 0.55.
* **Missing covariates.** The Data S1 code handles a missing biomarker
  (`-99`) by applying only the trajectory factor, for example `E1**THETA(5)`.
  That equals the full expression evaluated at the reference value, so a
  missing value should be imputed with the reference (65 kg, 3.5 g/dL, 9 mm/h,
  4.6) rather than handled in the model.
* **Baseline weight on Q and V2.** As in the Data S1 code, the predicted
  weight scales CL and V1, while Q and V2 are scaled by the pre-treatment
  weight.
* **Infusion counter between visits.** The paper defines the trajectories at
  infusion visits only. The vignette applies the visit `k + 1` values over the
  interval after infusion `k`, which reproduces the shape of Figure 2 (see
  above). A user who prefers to apply visit `k` values until the next
  infusion can set `CYCLE` to the infusion number of the most recent infusion.
* **IIV on V1, Q and V2.** The Data S1 `$OMEGA` holds these at 0, and Xiong
  2021 estimated IIV on CL only, so the model carries no eta for them.
* **Trajectory parameters.** The four Emax values were estimated by the
  authors on the biomarker data (Table S1), not on concentrations, and D50 was
  held at 1.1 because it could not be estimated. A refit of this model to PK
  data should hold the Emax values as well.
* **Antibodies to infliximab.** The ATI effect is part of the Xiong 2021 model
  and of the Data S1 code. Samuels 2025 did not give it a trajectory, because
  antibodies were rare in its cohorts. All simulations here assume no
  antibodies.
* **Figure 2 inputs.** The infusion duration (2 h here) and the pre-treatment
  albumin, ESR and nCD64 of the Figure 2 patient are not reported. The Table S1
  E0 values were used.
* **nCD64 percentage.** The Results and Figure 1d print -26.5% for the nCD64
  Emax of -0.362, which is -30.4%. The estimate is used as printed.
